items.instructions: Choose the word that is closest in meaning to the word on the left.

explanation.en: Luggage is the usual British word; baggage means the same, especially in American English.
To depart is the formal way to say leave a place.
A voyage is a long journey, usually by sea.
Lodging is a place to stay, and so is accommodation.
explanation.es: Accommodation no lleva plural en inglés británico.

explanation.en: A holidaymaker is a tourist: a person on holiday away from home.

items.instructions: Choose the word that matches each definition.

items.prompt: a detailed plan of the places you will visit on a journey

explanation.en: An itinerary lists where you will go and when.

items.prompt: the place at a border where officials check the goods you bring in

explanation.en: Customs officers can ask you to open your bags.
explanation.es: Customs (aduana) es siempre plural en este sentido.

items.prompt: a time when a train or flight leaves later than planned

explanation.en: A delay makes you wait longer than expected.

items.prompt: an object you buy to remember a place you have visited

explanation.en: A souvenir is something you keep as a memory of a trip.
explanation.es: Souvenir es el recuerdo que compras en un viaje.

items.prompt: a cheap place to stay, often with shared rooms

explanation.en: A hostel is a cheap place for travellers, often with shared dormitories.
explanation.es: Hostel no es "hostal": suele tener habitaciones compartidas.

items.instructions: Complete each sentence with the best word.

items.prompt: We need to ___ our hotel soon because August is very busy.

explanation.en: To book is to reserve a room or a seat in advance.

items.prompt: Our flight was ___ by two hours because of fog.

explanation.en: A delayed flight leaves later than planned; a cancelled one does not leave at all.

items.prompt: The train to Leeds leaves from ___ nine.

explanation.en: Trains arrive at and leave from a platform.

items.prompt: She has never been ___; she has not left the country once.

explanation.en: Abroad means in or to another country, and it has no preposition.
explanation.es: Se dice go abroad, no "go to abroad".

items.prompt: Remember to show your ___ at the check-in desk.

explanation.en: At an airport desk you show your passport as identification.
